_comment_history: 2026-09-25 Jax ruling: `public`'s original two commits (built before this manifest/pipeline existed) carried un-sanitized content and had to disappear from reachable history entirely -- not just get overwritten in a new commit's working tree. Every commitOntoPublic() call is therefore a single parentless (orphan) commit; `public`'s history is always exactly 1 commit deep, never a chain. Idempotency is unaffected -- it was already tree-hash-only, never parent-based (see commitOntoPublic's IDEMPOTENT check). Overridable per-invocation via the --orphan CLI flag, but this field is the standing default so an ordinary `node scripts/publish-public.cjs` run (no flags) still rebuilds an orphan commit, not a chain.

overlays._comment: Full-content replace. Used where the private->public difference is a hand-curated narrative (README) or a dense, coupled data-file edit (guard-canary.sh's roster/EXPECTED arithmetic; isolation-gate-contract.json's allow_prod roster remap + 3 report_only downgrades + mutation-set trim) that is safer to snapshot than to re-derive mechanically. Drift risk: if `main`'s OWN copy of one of these target paths changes after the overlay was hand-curated, the overlay snapshot can silently ship stale content -- see `overlayBaselines` below, which is the fail-closed check for exactly that (review FAB-2026-09-25-w11-w12-review.md MED-3).

overlayBaselines._comment: MED-3 fix (review FAB-2026-09-25-w11-w12-review.md MED-3): drift-detection baseline for each entry in `overlays` above. Value is the git blob sha of `main`'s OWN tracked file at that same path (`git rev-parse main:<path>`) as of the moment the hand-curated overlay content under publish-overrides/ (or README.public.md etc.) was last reviewed against it. checkOverlayDrift() in scripts/publish-public.cjs recomputes this sha at the start of every export and dies (before archiving/committing anything) if it no longer matches -- the private source at that path moved since the overlay was last reviewed, so the overlay snapshot may now be stale. After reviewing the diff at that path and refreshing the overlay content if needed, re-baseline with: `node scripts/publish-public.cjs --update-overlay-baselines` (rewrites only this section of this manifest; does not run the rest of the export pipeline).

replacements: _comment: each {file, findFile, replaceFile} pair does an exact, literal, whole-substring find/replace of findFile's content with replaceFile's content inside the exported copy of `file`. required=true (default) fails the export loudly if findFile's exact text is not found -- this is the forcing function that catches upstream drift instead of silently missing it.

sanitizeLiteralFallback._comment: LOW-1 fix (review FAB-2026-09-25-w11-w12-review.md LOW-1): the dynamic os.userInfo().username/os.hostname() rules below are only correct when the MACHINE RUNNING THE EXPORT is the machine whose identity needs scrubbing. On the CI runner (.github/workflows/publish-public.yml, ubuntu-latest) that is false -- the runner's own username/hostname are irrelevant; what needs to stay scrubbed is the AUTHOR's identity literals already baked into private-repo prose/strings/comments. This section is the hardcoded fallback so gate1_residualScan/step6_sanitize do not go blind on a host whose os.userInfo()/os.hostname() differ from the author's. Values taken from the author's own machine (see buildSanitizeRules() dynamic derivation on that machine, and the pre-existing per-file `replacements` patches for guards/bash-pipe-exitcode-watch.cjs, guards/pipe-gate-v2-acceptance.cjs, guards/pmm-bash-impression.cjs, which already strip these same literals from their known occurrences upstream of sanitize/gate1 -- this section is the union/fallback layer, not a replacement for those). This file is in `exclude` above (publish.manifest.json is never shipped to the public tree), so these literals never reach `public`.

sanitize._comment: Defense-in-depth regex scrub applied to every exported text file (not just the ones covered by replacements/overlays above). The username/hostname rules are the UNION of the running machine's os.userInfo().username / os.hostname() (dynamic, correct when export runs on the author's own machine) and the hardcoded literals in `sanitizeLiteralFallback` above (correct on any other host, e.g. CI) -- see that section's comment for why both are needed.

denylist._comment: 2026-09-26 W22-U1 (codex #1/#11/#13/#14, Opus defense unit U1) -- two lists consumed ONLY by GATE4 (scripts/publish-public.cjs gate4_finalTreeScan), an independently-coded scanner over the FINAL committed git tree's raw blob bytes (git ls-tree + git cat-file), never buildSanitizeRules()'s replacement loop -- see that function's own comment for why 'sanitize and scan share the same incomplete rules' must not be able to happen again. `identityLiterals` restates (as plain literal/word patterns, not the capture-group regexes step6_sanitize uses) the same identity strings sanitize.rules above already redacts, so GATE4 independently re-checks that redaction actually worked. `internalNames` is the class of private codenames/tags that have NO redaction rule at all by design (KNOWN-PROBLEMS.md is fully excluded; the two hooks/*.sh hits are fixed via literal `replacements` above) -- GATE4 fails the export if ANY of them ever reappears in the final tree, from any source (a future edit, a new file, a reverted patch). `match`: 'substring' (bare containment) or 'word' (ASCII \b-bounded, for short tokens like 'Dee'/'Jax' that would otherwise collide with ordinary English words like 'deep'). `caseSensitive`: default false; 'Jax' is true per 2026-09-26 W22-U1 spec (it is the author's real git user.name literal, not a generic OS-derived value, so it is not folded case-insensitively the way jax-x/JaxStuuu are).

binaryAllowlist: _comment: 2026-09-26 W22-U1 -- glob patterns (same tiny matcher as exclude/excludeExceptions) naming the only paths GATE4 permits to contain a NUL byte in the final tree (e.g. a shipped font/image/PDF asset). Empty today -- this repo currently ships zero binary files (0 symlinks, 0 NUL-containing blobs per the codex/Opus review's own clean-surface findings) -- so any NUL-containing blob dies the export until a maintainer deliberately adds its path here.

publicPathSnapshot._comment: 2026-09-26 W22-U1 (codex #4/#14, Opus U1 'path allowlist snapshot') -- `file` is a repo-relative (or, for tests, absolute) path to a newline-joined list of every path GATE5 (scripts/publish-public.cjs gate5_pathSnapshot) expects in the final exported tree. Both sides are ordered with a case-insensitive sort key for stable diffing, but the pass/fail check itself is an EXACT (case-preserving) full-array comparison -- this is what catches BOTH an ordinary added/removed path AND a same-count case-ONLY rename (a pure lowercase-folded compare would treat e.g. docs/README.md -> docs/Readme.md as unchanged), while still closing the case-variant exclude-glob escape, codex #4 (e.g. a stray `Scripts/x.cjs` next to excluded `scripts/**`), since that is simply an extra array entry either way. Re-baseline after a deliberate path-set change with: `node scripts/publish-public.cjs --update-path-snapshot --reason "<why>"` (prints the added/removed diff, refuses to run without --reason).
